summary: Chippewa County, WI steel tower on Flambeau Ridge, built 1931-32 and moved 1935-36; standing in 2019 but fenced on private summit land.

facts.design: 100-foot steel observation tower with a six-foot steel cab at the top

access.note: Summit land is privately owned; radio towers are fenced off to keep the public out; Tower Road is the only legal route to the summit area.

visit.trail_note: No marked trails to the summit; exploring beyond the road's end needs the property owner's permission.

events.note: Foundation laid by October 1931; completed the following spring
A tower man was on the job in May 1932
Tower watch reported fires starting near County Trunk M, close to Foster Lake; wardens and firefighters arrived in time
Moved farther north to a higher point; the move was under way in September 1935 and the tower was on its new site by April 1936
Wisconsin's 2015 announcement that lookout towers would close in 2016, per SummitPost; the sources do not record a specific closure for this tower

corrections.why: The value is a blank placeholder carried over from the source's 'Chippewa County - __-__-3' line, not an agency name. The 1931 and 1935 reports name the Wisconsin conservation commission.

notes_for_editor: Two sources disagree on timing: SummitPost says a 2015 announcement set closure for 2016, while WJFW says the towers still in use were decommissioned in 2015. Both are kept in the story; not reconciled. Location is unresolved: FFLA lists a separate 'first' Flambeau Ridge site, marked Gone, at 45.28101, -91.20750, about 0.7 km east of the standing tower's record coordinates. The 1935 report says the tower moved north, but the standing coordinates sit south of that site, so we could not tell which site the 1931-35 tower used. Record coordinates left unchanged. Access and visit facts come from SummitPost (2019) and are not confirmed for today. A 1975 report of a fall from the tower names a private person, so it is left out. Used 1 web search and about 5 page reads.
